title: Categorification of a small simplicial shape
statement: Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] for infinity-category, universe, and smallness conventions. For every small simplicial set $K$ there is a small infinity category $K^{\mathrm{cat}}$ and a categorical equivalence $K\to K^{\mathrm{cat}}$, functorially up to coherent equivalence, such that for every infinity category $\mathcal C$ restriction gives an equivalence of infinity categories $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{cat}},\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. Here $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ is the simplicial internal Hom, whose $n$-simplices are maps $K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$. Infinity categories are simplicial sets with fillers for inner horns. Smallness of $K^{\mathrm{cat}}$ is in the same universe as that of $K$. Categorical equivalence has the homotopy-category testing meaning stated in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure].

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 (Joyal model structure) and Theorem 2.4.6.1 (its fibrant objects), Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Proposition 1.2.7.3 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Work in the universe $\mathcal U$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Define $K_0=K$. Given $K_r$, let $T_r$ be the set of triples $(n,i,a)$ with $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$, and a simplicial map $a:\Lambda_i^n\to K_r$. Attach one $\Delta^n$ for every such triple, using the pushout
$$K_{r+1}=K_r\amalg_{\coprod_{(n,i,a)\in T_r}\Lambda_i^n}\coprod_{(n,i,a)\in T_r}\Delta^n.$$
Construct this degreewise as the disjoint union modulo the identifications prescribed by $a$. Simplicial operators on the quotient are well defined because $a$ commutes with them. Each $K_r\to K_{r+1}$ is degreewise injective: in a set pushout along an injection no two distinct elements of the other summand are identified. Put $R(K)=\operatorname{colim}_{r\in\mathbf N}K_r$, degreewise the union along these injections, and let $i_K:K\to R(K)$ be the inclusion. All indexing sets $T_r$, quotients, and the countable union belong to $\mathcal U$, so $R(K)$ is small in that same universe.

source.place: Agent-written explicit inner-horn small-object construction underlying the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1 (online PDF p.108) and the inner-anodyne replacement in Corollary 2.2.5.4

proof.text: Every map $a:\Lambda_i^n\to R(K)$ factors through some $K_r$. Indeed the horn is generated by its finitely many included faces of $\Delta^n$; choose a stage containing their images and then a common stage for all their face-compatibility equations. The equations already hold there because all transition maps are injective. Degeneracies introduce no further choices or relations. The attached simplex indexed by $(n,i,a)$ in $K_{r+1}$ fills this horn in $R(K)$. Thus $R(K)$ is a quasicategory. Moreover let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration, with maps $u:K\to E$ and $v:R(K)\to B$ satisfying $pu=vi_K$. Start with $\ell_0=u$. If $p\ell_r=v|_{K_r}$, then for each attached simplex $d_t:\Delta^n\to K_{r+1}$ labelled by $t=(n,i,a)$ the maps $\ell_r a:\Lambda_i^n\to E$ and $vd_t:\Delta^n\to B$ give a commuting inner-horn square. Choose its filler, which restricts to $\ell_r a$ and lies over $vd_t$. The fillers and $\ell_r$ agree on the attached horns, so the pushout gives $\ell_{r+1}$ extending $\ell_r$ with $p\ell_{r+1}=v|_{K_{r+1}}$. Their union is a simplicial map $\ell:R(K)\to E$ with $\ell i_K=u$ and $p\ell=v$. Thus $i_K$ has the left lifting property against every inner fibration. This also defines explicitly the term inner anodyne, using its lifting-class convention in [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. This recursive lifting argument works in any larger ambient universe containing the test inner fibration; it does not require the test objects to be small in the original universe of $K$.

source.place: Explicit finite-generation and recursive lifting argument for the small-object construction; HTT proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, online PDF p.108

proof.text: In the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], each inner horn inclusion is a trivial cofibration. Hence every Joyal fibration is an inner fibration, by its lifting property against trivial cofibrations. Step 2 therefore shows that $i_K$ has the left lifting property against every Joyal fibration. The weak factorization system (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) in that node makes $i_K$ a trivial cofibration, hence a categorical equivalence. Set $K^{\mathrm{cat}}=R(K)$. This supplies the required categorical equivalence without treating the ordinary homotopy category $hK$ as the categorification.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Lemma 2.2.5.2; weak-factorization-system characterization applied to the constructed horn inclusion

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be any quasicategory, enlarging the ambient universe to contain it while keeping the index shape in $\mathcal U$. For any simplicial set $A$, define $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)_m=\operatorname{Hom}(A\times\Delta^m,\mathcal C)$, with operators given by precomposition in the second factor. A horn in this internal Hom is the same data as a map $A\times\Lambda_i^n\to\mathcal C$: glue its face maps along their intersections, degreewise. The inclusion $A\times\Lambda_i^n\to A\times\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne by the pushout-product theorem [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], applied to the inner horn inclusion and $\varnothing\to A$, and swapping product factors. An inner horn inclusion has the required left lifting property simply by the definition of inner fibration. Since $\mathcal C\to *$ is an inner fibration, this map extends to $A\times\Delta^n$. Consequently $\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory, in particular for $A=K$ and $A=K^{\mathrm{cat}}$.

source.place: Corollary 2.3.2.4 and the adjoint lifting argument of Corollary 2.3.2.5; Notation 1.2.7.2

proof.text:
Write $Q=K^{\mathrm{cat}}$ and $p=i_K^*:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. A lifting problem for $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ against $p$ is, by the degreewise internal-Hom description, a map
$$ (Q\times\partial\Delta^n)\amalg_{K\times\partial\Delta^n}(K\times\Delta^n)\longrightarrow\mathcal C.$$
The map from this pushout to $Q\times\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], since step 2 proved $i_K$ inner anodyne and the boundary inclusion is degreewise injective. The inner fibration $\mathcal C\to *$ therefore provides the required extension and hence the lift. This includes $n=0$, whose boundary is empty, and gives surjectivity on vertices. Thus $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration in precisely the boundary-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Corollaries 2.3.2.4-2.3.2.5, specialized to inner-anodyne i_K and the boundary inclusion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the trivial Kan fibration $p$ from step 5. It has the right lifting property against every degreewise injection, hence against every Joyal cofibration by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The weak factorization system (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) of that node then makes $p$ a Joyal trivial fibration, in particular a categorical equivalence. Step 4 has verified that both its source and target are quasicategories. This proves the asserted equivalence of infinity categories for the actual restriction map, including transformations and higher simplices.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1; Proposition 1.2.7.3(3), here proved for the constructed inner-anodyne replacement using the stronger trivial-Kan restriction

proof.text: For a map $f:K\to L$, define $f_0=f$ and define $f_{r+1}$ on the old summand by $f_r$ and on the simplex indexed by $(n,i,a)$ as the identity simplex in the summand indexed by $(n,i,f_ra)$. These maps agree on each horn, hence induce the pushout map. They preserve identities and composition on every summand, so the induced union maps make $R$ a functor with the natural inclusion $i:\mathrm{id}\to R$. For each $f$, the equality $R(f)i_K=i_Lf$ gives the strictly commuting restriction square after applying $\operatorname{Fun}(-,\mathcal C)$. For a composable string $K_0\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_q}K_q$, the string $R(K_0)\xrightarrow{R(f_1)}\cdots\xrightarrow{R(f_q)}R(K_q)$ has composite edges $R(f_s\cdots f_{r+1})=R(f_s)\cdots R(f_{r+1})$ for $r<s$. Deleting a vertex composes these arrows and repeating a vertex inserts $R(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, so these strings form compatible simplices under every face and degeneracy. The equalities $R(f)i_K=i_Lf$ give a natural transformation on these entire diagrams. Thus the construction and restriction comparisons are strictly functorial, which supplies the requested functoriality up to coherent equivalence. If $f$ is a categorical equivalence, two-out-of-three and the two maps $i_K,i_L$ show $R(f)$ is one too. The definition in step 4 gives exactly the stated formula for all $n$-simplices.
